dedupe_keys.name: ethical smart grid reinforcement learning environment

description: Ethical Smart Grid is a Gym-style environment for reinforcement-learning experiments on electricity sharing among simulated households. Agents choose consumption and distribution actions while the reward design considers comfort and fairness between residents. The households, demand pattern and simulation horizon are configured for an experiment; the package does not represent a named utility grid or measured household dataset. The public repository licence file states MIT, although the GitHub classifier returns NOASSERTION. It can help test how different objectives alter simulated allocation in an electricity microgrid. A caveat is explicit in the JOSS paper: the simplified environment is not suitable for deploying trained agents directly to a real smart grid. Physical network constraints and institutional rules must be added for operational conclusions. No directly related catalogue record was established. The paper, own repository and licence were read without training an agent. Its spatial coverage is a configurable synthetic household group, and its temporal coverage is the experiment horizon, not a historical period.
name: Ethical Smart Grid reinforcement-learning environment
notes: G5 G5-0724. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
